r.정치 구도: The People's Action Party has never lost power since self-government began in 1959. That held after 1965, when Singapore separated from the Malaysian federation and became independent. Elections are held regularly and opposition parties exist, but in the May 2025 general election the ruling party took 87 of 97 seats. Under the group constituency system, candidates run as teams that must include a member of a minority group. In a country where Chinese, Malay and Indian communities live side by side, this protects minority seats, and it also raises the bar for opposition parties with fewer people. The president is directly elected, but real power lies with the prime minister, and the president's main role is to approve or block spending from the national reserves. Housing prices, the cost of living and foreign workers are issues in every election.

t.why: Sitting at the end of the Strait of Malacca, which links the Indian and Pacific oceans, it grew into one of the busiest ports in the world. Its trade is about three times the size of its economy, so it is among the first to feel it when big countries raise trade barriers. It is not a US ally, yet it lets American warships and aircraft use its bases, and it is closely tied to China through trade and investment. Its reputation for not taking sides is why the first US-North Korea summit was held there in 2018, and why defense chiefs from around the world gather there each year for the Shangri-La Dialogue. It was one of the five countries that founded ASEAN in 1967. Part of its drinking water is piped in from Johor in Malaysia under an agreement that ends in 2061, so it is expanding recycled water and desalination.
t.rel: A small city-state on the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia, famous for balanced diplomacy: security cooperation with the United States alongside close economic ties with China.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1975. A free trade agreement took effect in 2006, and in 2023 the Digital Partnership Agreement, South Korea's first digital trade pact, came into force and aligned rules on data and e-commerce. In November 2025, the 50th anniversary of ties, they upgraded the relationship to a strategic partnership, and in March 2026 they agreed to open talks on updating the free trade agreement. The Marina Bay Sands hotel, with a ship-shaped park resting on three towers, was built by South Korea's Ssangyong Engineering & Construction, and Korean builders have also worked on the city's subway lines and roads. In 2023 Hyundai Motor Group opened an innovation center there that builds electric cars while testing new production methods.
t.know: Singapore has reclaimed land from the sea, growing by about a quarter since independence.
etext: Its port handles more transshipment cargo, moved from one ship to another, than any other in the world. A ship that calls there can refuel, get repairs and arrange insurance and financing in one place. A large project is under way to bring the scattered terminals together at Tuas in the west.
Stable laws and low taxes draw Asia's banks, asset managers and private fortunes. State investment company Temasek and GIC, a sovereign wealth fund, invest the nation's savings around the world.

For all its lack of land, it has many chip, pharmaceutical and precision equipment plants. Refineries and petrochemical plants are clustered on Jurong Island, built on reclaimed land, so a country with no oil of its own exports petroleum products.

It imports nearly all its water, food and energy. The birth rate is very low and the country leans on foreign workers, which feeds discontent over housing prices and jobs. Living on trade, it is shaken directly by US-China tensions and tariff fights.
